clue.text: Indian chief sitting on the political fence

definitions.meaning: an Algonquian word for a chief or great man
describes one who stays neutral and refuses to commit to a party line

explanation.surface: A tribal leader declines to take sides in an election.
explanation.definitionFit: The word came from an Algonquian title for a leader and was later applied in American politics to independents who will not take sides.

clue.text: Attacked by the rabble-bombed to bits

indicators.note: blown to bits means broken apart, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Set on by a crowd, then blown apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bits' rearranges the letters of BOMBED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being crowded round and set upon by a disorderly mob is what the past participle describes.

clue.text: Pig a little one carried by old railway

indicators.note: a passenger carried by a train sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: GER was the Great Eastern Railway, a pre-1923 British company
a runt is the smallest of a litter

explanation.surface: A piglet transported on a bygone railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Eastern Railway ran in eastern England until 1923, one of many old companies with three-letter initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A grunter is an informal name for a hog, from the noise it makes.

clue.text: Neat, how the United Nations did without an instrument

parts.note: UN is the abbreviation for the United Nations

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: taken as written
a lute is a plucked string instrument

explanation.surface: Plainly, how the UN managed after losing a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. 'Neat' is drink taken with nothing added, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit served neat has no water or mixer in it, unwatered.

clue.text: They're more the Pompadour than the Helen type

definitions.text: They're more the Pompadour than the Helen type

parts.words: They're more the Pompadour than the Helen type
parts.note: Madame de Pompadour was a woman of the French capital, while Helen of Troy merely eloped with the Trojan prince of the same name

explanation.surface: Some women resemble Louis XV's mistress more than the beauty of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen belonged to Paris the Trojan prince; Madame de Pompadour belonged to Paris the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who live in the French capital, as Madame de Pompadour did, are its female citizens.

clue.text: Boar's Head. Drew bath, ready for a dip

indicators.note: the head of the word Boar's is its opening letter

parts.note: drew a bath means ran one
a tub is a bath

explanation.surface: An inn called the Boar's Head where someone runs a bath before a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boar's Head' looks like an inn sign, but 'Head' takes the first letter of 'Boar's'. A bran tub is the British fairground lucky dip, a tub of bran with prizes buried in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The prizes in this tub wait for children to plunge a hand in, a lucky dip.

clue.text: Stop here for refreshment

definitions.meaning: a pub counter or saloon where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Pull in at this place for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to block, and is also a place serving drinks.

clue.text: A personal anthology may contain records

definitions.text: A personal anthology may contain records

parts.words: A personal anthology may contain records
parts.note: a scrapbook of cuttings or photos is a personal collection, and gramophone discs come in the same kind of folder

explanation.surface: A private collection of writings could include documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'records' reads as documents but means gramophone discs, which were sold in sleeved books of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank book for photographs or cuttings is a personal collection, and the name also covers a set of recordings.

clue.text: The big noise this journal made

definitions.text: The big noise this journal made

parts.words: The big noise this journal made
parts.note: The Times, where the clue appears, has long been nicknamed The ..., so its own noise is the roar of a storm

explanation.surface: The great fuss that this newspaper caused.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times was nicknamed 'The Thunderer' for its forceful editorials in the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The loud rumble after lightning is the big noise, and a Thunderer makes it.

clue.text: What Lady Chatterley's Lover was bound to become

definitions.text: What Lady Chatterley's Lover was bound to become

parts.words: What Lady Chatterley's Lover was bound to become
parts.note: Lawrence's novel was the subject of a famous 1960 obscenity trial, and a bound volume belongs on a shelf for books

explanation.surface: The fate that D. H. Lawrence's notorious novel could not escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Chatterley's Lover was tried for obscenity in 1960, making it a famous legal case about a book; 'bound' means both certain and given covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as two words it is a lawsuit about a volume; as one, a piece of furniture that holds bound volumes.

clue.text: Rub lender the wrong way ? His error

definitions.text: Rub lender the wrong way ? His error

indicators.note: rubbing the wrong way suggests these letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who annoys the person lending him money has made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' rearranges RUB and LENDER; the whole clue then describes the clumsy man whose mistake it is to irritate his creditor.
explanation.definitionFit: One who offends the very person funding him is making a bungle, the act of a bungler.

clue.text: Sylvie's little brother embraces one in France

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bro is a shortened, familiar form of brother
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A girl's younger sibling hugs someone on a trip to France.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's novel Sylvie and Bruno pairs the girl with her small brother, so 'Sylvie's' points to him while 'little brother' also supplies BRO.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's Sylvie and Bruno, the fairy child Sylvie's companion is her younger sibling of this name.

clue.text: Former tax return makes us crack up

parts.note: ex is a prefix for a former partner or holder

indicators.note: a return is a coming back, so the word for tax is read backwards

parts.note: lot is an old word for a levy, as in scot and lot

explanation.surface: Getting a refund of an old tax leaves us in fits of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack up' here is the verb to praise highly, not to laugh or break down.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack something up is to speak of it in glowing terms, to praise it.

clue.text: Having misplaced compass I'd go in this fits-and-starts way

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A walker who has lost his compass wanders erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges COMPASS and ID, the letters of I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irregular and intermittent proceeds by fits and starts, in jerks.

clue.text: " Greenery-yallery, Grosvenor Gallery " ?

parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience mocks the artistic young man of the 1880s in exactly these words

explanation.surface: A quotation from a comic opera about a fashionable art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: In Patience, Bunthorne is 'a greenery-yallery, Grosvenor Gallery, foot-in-the-grave young man', a lampoon of the 1880s cult of beauty led by Wilde; the Grosvenor Gallery in London showed its painters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Patience satirises the artistic movement devoted to beauty, so it describes that kind of pose.

clue.text: Twin baby boys who fight with each other ?

definitions.text: Twin baby boys who fight with each other ?

parts.words: Twin baby boys who fight with each other ?
parts.note: squabbling twin boys are siblings with their fists up, while the phrase really means comrades who serve together in war

explanation.surface: Two infant sons who are always scrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who fight side by side are called comrades, close as siblings, with weapons.

clue.text: Wants fresh wine — it's compulsory

parts.note: to want something is to need it
must is newly pressed grape juice before fermentation

explanation.surface: Someone longs for new wine and insists on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'needs must when the devil drives'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase says necessity leaves no choice, which is the same as saying something is obligatory.

clue.text: What tramways did with old vehicles

definitions.text: What tramways did with old vehicles

parts.words: What tramways did with old vehicles
parts.note: a tram line ran its carriages, the cars, so it put them to use, while the phrase also names second-hand motors

explanation.surface: How the tram companies treated their ageing carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramways employed their trams, called cars; the same words name second-hand motors for sale.

clue.text: Famous last words made good at Mr Walker's request

definitions.text: Famous last words made good at Mr Walker's request

parts.words: Famous last words made good at Mr Walker's request
parts.note: a cobbler shapes shoes on a last, and a man who walks a lot asks for his footwear repaired at sole and heel

explanation.surface: A dying man's well-known final words come true when a Mr Walker asks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' is the cobbler's shoe form, not final words, and 'Mr Walker' is anyone who wears out shoes; the phrase also means well provided for.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear made good by a cobbler has new soles and new heels fitted, the repair a walker needs.

clue.text: The end of a flight

parts.note: an aircraft touching down ends its journey, and a level platform ends a set of stairs

explanation.surface: An aeroplane arriving at its destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a plane journey and also a set of stairs; both end at the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching down ends an air journey, and the platform at the top of stairs ends a staircase.

clue.text: Communication-it is involved with sleep

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A message tangled up with someone's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges IT and SLEEP; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter, especially a formal one or one in the New Testament, is a written message.

clue.text: Pictures projected in a girl's hair ?

definitions.meaning: transparencies shown on a screen by a projector
hair clips worn to hold hair in place

explanation.surface: Images being beamed onto a young woman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names photographic transparencies for a projector and also clips that hold hair back.

clue.text: Forms the foundation of a meal for social eaters ?

definitions.text: Forms the foundation of a meal for social eaters ?

parts.words: Forms the foundation of a meal for social eaters ?
parts.note: the plates and dishes underlie a formal meal, and a sociable group of diners is itself such a set

explanation.surface: Something that is the basis of a meal for people who like to eat together.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching service of plates and dishes is what an evening meal is laid on, and a party of diners is a set of them.

clue.text: Buck up it's a quarter after time

parts.note: E is East, one of the four quarters or compass points
late means past the appointed time

explanation.surface: Cheer up, it's fifteen minutes past the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' reads as a quarter of an hour, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck someone up is to cheer or raise their spirits.

clue.text: Quiet, yet it may be full of spirit

definitions.text: it may be full of spirit
definitions.meaning: a distilling apparatus holds the spirit being made

explanation.surface: Calm, though perhaps lively underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means calm, also nevertheless, and is also the apparatus for distilling whisky or gin.

clue.text: She ain't a bad girl

indicators.note: a bad version of something is a corrupted one, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: She is not a naughty girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges only the letters of ain't, giving ANIT, and the final A stays where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's first name, so the solver needs any female name.

clue.text: Checked again, but still told

definitions.meaning: counted a second time, as votes are

explanation.surface: Votes were checked once more, yet the story was still told.
explanation.definitionFit: The word splits as re-counted, counted once more, and also means narrated, as of a tale.

clue.text: Eminence rising to decay

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or high point

explanation.surface: A high place climbing towards ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses TOR in this down entry; 'Eminence' looks like a cardinal's title but is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decompose or go bad.

clue.text: Government agents in tax division

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, held between its letters

parts.note: set means impose or assess, as a tax is set on goods
G-men are FBI agents in American slang, from Government men

explanation.surface: Federal officers working in the tax department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax division' reads like a government department, but 'division' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A part cut off from a whole is a section or portion of it.

clue.text: Post employs four

parts.note: the word Post is spelt with four characters of the alphabet, and post means the mail that is delivered

explanation.surface: The Post Office takes on four staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is made of written messages, and the word Post itself uses four characters of the alphabet.
